projects.title: Reclaim Creative — Stabilize
projects.description: Assistive drawing system that filters essential tremor in real time, letting artists with hand tremors draw via a robotic plotter.
projects.longDescription: A team capstone project addressing essential tremor, a condition affecting over 10 million Americans. Two VL53L7CX time-of-flight sensors triangulate hand position; an IIR low-pass filter on a Nucleo-L476RG strips tremor frequencies (5–12 Hz) while preserving intentional motion. Filtered coordinates drive a custom Cartesian plotter with NEMA 17 stepper motors at 80 steps/mm accuracy, enabling fluid artistic expression regardless of tremor severity.

projects.title: Bar Shift Manager Mobile App
projects.description: Cross-platform mobile application for bartenders to calculate tips, balance cash drawers, and track shift notes.
projects.longDescription: Professional React Native application built with TypeScript and Expo. Features a sophisticated tip calculator with hourly rate distribution based on staff hours worked, cash drawer balancing with over/short tracking, and shift notes for inventory and incident reporting. Designed for real-world bar operations with an intuitive mobile-first interface. Data is stored locally for financial privacy with plans to sync operational notes to backend management systems.

projects.title: Automated Louvers for Passive Climate Control
projects.description: Programmable automated cooling system for sustainable home and commercial development using STM32 microcontroller.
projects.longDescription: Comprehensive graduate research project completed as part of the ENGR 696 coursework. This project demonstrates advanced electrical engineering principles, analysis, and practical implementation. Features automated louver control for passive climate regulation and energy efficiency in residential and commercial buildings. Full technical write-up and documentation available.

projects.title: TI LM-21215 Buck Converter Evaluation Board
projects.description: Custom evaluation board for the Texas Instruments LM21215 IC, designed as a 5V to 1.8V step-down DC-DC converter capable of supplying 5A with tight ripple and transient specifications.
projects.longDescription: Designed, built, and tested a buck converter evaluation board using the TI LM21215 synchronous buck controller for ENGR-455. The board steps down 5V to 1.8V at up to 5A, meeting strict design targets: <30% inductor current ripple, <1% voltage ripple at input and output, and >50° phase margin. All components were hand-soldered using 0805 or larger packages with test points at the input, output, switch node, P-good, and enable pins. Testing revealed inductor saturation at high loads attributed to thermal effects, and transient noise traced to input capacitor over-selection — resolved by reducing capacitance from 150µF to 100µF. Measured load-step voltage droop was 35mV vs. a 26.5mV theoretical target. Phase margin was verified via TI WEBench at 73°, exceeding the 50° requirement.

projects.title: FPGA Based LED Dimmer System
projects.description: Automated LED dimmer system using FPGA with pulse width and pulse frequency modulation.
projects.longDescription: Developed as part of the Open Avenues Build Foundation program. Programmed an FPGA in Verilog to control LED dimmers using pulse width modulation (PWM) and pulse frequency modulation techniques. Utilized Icarus and GTKWave simulation software for testing and verification. Implemented the system on an Efinix Xyloni development board. Produced a comprehensive presentation on the process, results, and projected applications of FPGA-based PWM signal control.
